can_do_statement: Can use 'but' to join a limited range of common adjectives, after 'be'.

ontology.mental_model: contrastive layering of attributes on one entity

negatives: He bought milk but forgot eggs.
She is a teacher but works late.
positives: The weather was cloudy but fine.
It was cheap but beautiful.

can_do_statement: Can use 'and' to join a limited range of common adjectives.

negatives: He opened the door and walked in.
positives: The teachers are very nice and friendly.
It is big and comfortable.

can_do_statement: Can use an increasing range of compound adjectives ('up-to-date', 'state-of-the-art')

ontology.mental_model: hyphen as glue for a single complex attribute

positives: The report is up-to-date.
We use state-of-the-art technology.

can_do_statement: Can use commas and 'and' to join more than two adjectives, after 'be'.
guideword: FORM: COMBINING MORE THAN TWO ADJECTIVES

ontology.mental_model: list of attributes closed by and
ontology.pedagogical_hook: list them, then close the list

positives: She is beautiful, intelligent, funny and reliable.
He is tall, thin and friendly.

can_do_statement: Can use 'and' to repeat a comparative adjective to indicate change over time, usually after 'become' or get. ► adjectives: comparatives
guideword: FORM: COMBINING THE SAME COMPARATIVE ADJECTIVE WITH 'AND'

positives: The room became hotter and hotter.
The weather got colder and colder.

can_do_statement: Can use a comma to combine two adjectives used before the noun, following the usual order of adjective types.

positives: Its huge, black screen was impressive.
They bought a big, red car yesterday.

can_do_statement: Can use a limited range of compound adjectives ('good-looking', 'well-known')

ontology.mental_model: hyphen joins two roots into one trait

positives: He is good-looking.
She is well-known.

can_do_statement: Can use 'and' to join a limited range of comparative adjectives.► adjectives: comparatives

positives: He is taller and stronger than before.
This car is cheaper and faster.

can_do_statement: Can use adjective phrases to modify nouns.

ontology.mental_model: noun narrowed by a participial phrase
ontology.pedagogical_hook: which one? the one built when

positives: The cake made yesterday tasted great.
The letter sent last week arrived.

can_do_statement: Can use a wide range of compound adjectives ('open-minded', 'above-mentioned', 'well-to-do', 'jaw-dropping')

ontology.mental_model: hyphen compresses a clause into a trait

positives: She is open-minded.
It was jaw-dropping.

can_do_statement: Can use a list of adjectives in ellipted clauses before and after a noun, to give focus. ► focus

ontology.mental_model: fronted attribute list spotlights the referent

negatives: He was imaginative, kind and friendly.
He walked in tall and dark.
positives: Imaginative, kind and friendly, he was loved.
Tall, dark and handsome, he walked in.

can_do_statement: Can combine more complex, lengthy strings of adjectives, joining the last two adjectives with 'and'.

ontology.mental_model: long attribute chain closed by and

positives: She is timid, shy and vulnerable.
The society is materialistic, greedy and shallow.
